items.title: Trizbort: Recast user guide
items.text:
Trizbort: Recast is a map editor for interactive fiction. Draw rooms and the ways between them as you play, or let Automap draw the map for you from the game's transcript. Recast runs on Windows, Linux and macOS.

Automapping a small game. The token shows where you are, and the panel on the right follows the game.

Press F1 in Recast to open this guide.

items.title: Older versions
items.text: Recast opens and saves the same .trizbort maps as the original Trizbort. The guide to the original app and the Windows-only Trizbort 2 is still here: Using Trizbort (the original app, and Trizbort 2). It goes into more depth on some things that work the same way in Recast.

items.title: Help and feedback
items.text: Found a bug, or have an idea? Open an issue. The full list of changes is in the changelog.

items.title: Automap
items.text:
Back to the guide

Automap draws the map while you play. It reads the game's transcript, the record of everything you typed and everything the game said, and adds each room and the way you went. You can change the map as it goes.

items.title: Transcripts
items.text:
Most interpreters can save a transcript. In the game, type SCRIPT (or SCRIPT ON) and choose a file name. Transcripts are plain text files, often ending .txt, .scr or .log:

>LOOK
West of House
You are standing in an open field west of a white house, with a boarded front door.
There is a small mailbox here.

>NORTHEAST
North of House
You are facing the north side of a white house.

Automap works best when you also:

  1. Type VERBOSE, so the game describes each room every time you enter it. Automap uses descriptions to tell rooms with the same name apart.
  2. Type LOOK once the transcript has started, so automap can see where you are.

Automap can follow the game live as you play, or read a finished transcript afterwards. Interpreters such as Windows Frotz, Gargoyle, Glulxe and Git write the transcript as you go, so automap keeps up; some only write every few turns, so the map runs a little behind.

items.title: Starting
items.text:
Choose Project > Automap > Start Automap... and pick the transcript. It's often best to start with an empty map, but you can open a map you automapped before and carry on: handy for a game you play over several weeks.

  • Guess possible exits reads "To the east..." in a room's description and draws a short stub for each way out you haven't tried yet. It takes them away if you find you can't go that way. It can guess wrong ("To the east is an impassable pile of rubble"), so turn it off if you'd rather.
  • Tidy the map as you go moves nearby rooms aside to make space for new ones. See Tidying.
  • Assume joins go both ways (on): going north from one room to another also maps south as the way back. If it turns out to lead somewhere else, automap moves it. Turn it off for a maze of twisty passages.
  • Start processing from the end maps only what you play from now on, leaving the map as it is. Leave it off and automap reads the whole transcript.
  • Play the transcript a move at a time starts paused, to step through an old transcript.
  • Hover over the ⓘ beside an option for more about it.
  • Commands: type see lamp in the game and automap adds a lamp to the room; tb region Cellars puts the room in a region. The game won't understand them, and doesn't need to. Automap doesn't check the game's reply, so a typing mistake ends up on the map; delete it there. Change the commands to whatever you like.

items.title: The automap panel
items.text:
While automap runs, its controls sit in a panel beside the map.

  • The transcript's name is at the top. Open Folder shows it in its folder.
  • Where you are names the room you're in. On the map that room glows and carries a token, like a playing piece on a board. If automap has lost track, drag the token onto the right room, or right-click the room and choose Automap: I'm Here. The dot beside the name is green while automap is mapping, amber while it isn't changing the map, and grey in the dark. Centre on Current Room moves the map to it.
  • Somewhere not on the map? Add Current Room puts it on the map beside the room you came from.
  • Transcript steps through the game: Next Move (F10), Previous Move (F9), which goes back without changing the map, and Pause. "Move 12 of 4,567" counts the commands you typed.
  • Play to the End (F5) plays every move left, showing its progress, and then follows the game as you play. The map can't be changed until it's done or you pause. With 20 or more moves left it asks first.
  • Go Live appears when you've stepped to the end of the transcript and carried on playing: choose it to map each move as you play it.
  • Mapping / Tracking only: tracking follows you round without changing the map. Use it to step through and check automap follows the rooms you expect; put the map right if not, then switch back to Mapping.
  • The little game screen shows the game so far. Click it for a bigger one you can copy from, or drag the panel's left edge to widen it.
  • The ⚙ changes the settings while automap runs.

However far out you zoom, the token stays big enough to find:

Choose a different token, or load your own picture, in App Settings > Map.

items.title: Which room is it?
items.text:
Games are full of rooms with the same name: "Maze", "Corridor". Automap tells them apart by the map first (where the way you went leads), then by their descriptions. When it still can't tell, it asks:

Each room is listed with its subtitle and objects, and the ways out of it where that's what tells it apart. Click one to see its description, and the map behind the dialog shows it. Pick the room you're in, or . A room the game now describes differently (the Twopit Room once the beanstalk has grown) is the same room at another time: pick it, and automap remembers the new description too.

  • Cancel maps nothing for this move. Automap carries on from the next room it can place.
  • Don't ask again: make a best guess stops the questions for the rest of this run: the room whose description starts the same way, else a new room.

When automap decides for itself and it could be wrong, it says what it guessed and why:

Choose That's Right, or Wrong Room: Choose... to put it right.

items.title: A way out leads somewhere new
items.text:
You went east from the Hall to the Pantry before, and now east leads to the Kitchen. Automap stops and asks:

  • Both Are Right: the way leads to either, depending on something in the game, or they're one place at different times (a dry riverbed that floods once the dam is opened). Both joins stay. Next time automap goes by the room the game names.
  • 'Hall' Moves: the room is a lift or a vehicle. See Rooms that move.
  • A Different 'Hall': you were in another room with the same name. Automap adds it and moves the way you came in over to it.

A way back that automap only assumed isn't something you saw, so when it turns out to lead somewhere else, automap just puts it right.

items.title: Rooms that move
items.text:
A lift, a car or a train takes you with it: you get in, it moves, and you get out somewhere else. Choose 'Closet' Moves when automap asks, or tick Moves in the room's properties.

  • Automap adds a copy of the room at each place it stops, a stop, joined from the room by what moved it.
  • It asks What moved it?, listing the commands you typed in the room with its best guess picked. Choose Nothing I did for something that moves by itself (the join is labelled "(by itself)"), or Something else... to type it.
  • From then on automap works out which stop you're at from the way you go out, and asks nothing more as you ride up and down. Typing a command it knows moves you to the other stop straight away.
  • A moving room and its stops show a small blue sign with up and down arrows. Ctrl+click a stop to go to the room.
  • If automap didn't see the room move (you pulled the peg and walked out without going back), right-click the room and choose Room > Add Another Stop. Drag the new stop to where it went.
  • A join between stops labelled with the wrong command? Clear its label, or delete it, and automap asks again next time.

items.title: Splitting a room
items.text:
Found out a few moves later that one room on the map is really two places? Right-click it and choose Split Room.... Click each way in or out to move it to the new room.

The original is on the left with its objects, and the new room on the right. Moving only one half of a two-way join splits it into two one-way joins. If automap has you in the room, you're in the new one; if you're really in the original, right-click it and choose Automap: I'm Here.

items.title: Merging rooms
items.text: A place on the map twice? Select both rooms, the one to keep last, and choose Rooms > Merge Rooms. The other room's joins, descriptions and objects move onto the one you keep.

items.title: Rooms automap can't map
items.text: For a maze, or a room automap can't make sense of, tick Don't automap from here in its properties (or choose Automap > Disable Automap on This Room on its right-click menu). It shows a small amber "no entry" sign. While you're there automap maps nothing; when you come out it carries on, with a dotted "?" join for the way through if the room is new. Relabel the join when you've worked out the way.

items.title: Dark rooms
items.text: A heading that says it's too dark to see ("Darkness", "It is pitch black") isn't mapped as a room. When you light the lamp, the room you see is mapped as reached the way you came, and marked Dark.

items.title: Areas of their own
items.text: Some parts of a game feel like a map of their own, such as the inside of a house after the gardens. Select the first room of that part (the Foyer), right-click and choose Rooms > Move to a New Area.... The rooms move aside together, and their joins to the rooms left behind are split: drawn as a short stub at each end, labelled with the room at the other end ("to Front Porch"). They're still the same joins, so automap follows them, and maps new rooms in the new area. Click a stub's label to go to the room it names.

items.title: Copies of rooms
items.text: A room can stand for another: set Reference in its properties. It's drawn "To Front Porch", in the other room's look, and Ctrl+click goes there. A moving room's stops are copies too. A copy's right-click menu can go to the room it stands for, move its joins onto that room, or make it a room of its own.

items.title: Tidying
items.text:
With Tidy the map as you go on, after each move the rooms nearby shift so joins point the way their directions say, never run across a room, and cross each other as little as possible. The rooms slide to their new places, so you can follow where they went. A new room goes on the map straight away and the tidy follows a moment later, as its own undo step: undo a tidy you don't like and the new room stays where automap put it.

A room you've moved yourself stays where you put it, though it slides aside if a new room needs its place. To tidy the whole map, or just some rooms, choose Rooms > Tidy Map...: step by step keeps the map familiar, and the solver lays everything out again.

items.title: How automap reads the game
items.text:
Automap works things out from the text, and can be wrong. If it gets something wrong that it should have got right, let us know.

  • Room names are headings: short lines of words with capitals ("West of House"), grid references ("Y2"), or names with a part after a comma ("Garden, north"). It leaves off endings such as " (on the bed)" or ", under the table". Sometimes it takes the game's title for a room: delete it.
  • Moving: compass directions, up, down, in and out, with or without go or walk, and port, starboard, fore and aft (and their short forms). Up, down, in and out label their joins.
  • Anything else that takes you to a new room (xyzzy, enter boat) joins it from where you were, labelled with what you typed. Automap follows joins labelled with a command: type it again and it moves you along the join.
  • Joins it made: it remembers each way along a join, from which end, and whether you went that way or it only assumed it. The labels are drawn from those. A join you draw yourself, or whose labels or ends you change, is read from its labels and sides, so what you write is what counts.
  • Games it can't map: ones without a > prompt, or that don't give rooms names, or that move you about in their own ways.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Move with plain directions (north, n, up) where you can, especially the first time you go somewhere: automap places a room by the way you went to it. Go through a doorway to the north with north rather than in.
  • One command at a prompt. Automap can't tell which part of the reply goes with which of n. e. get lamp.
  • Move rooms around as you like: automap only cares about the joins. Rooms you move yourself stay put.
  • Delete anything automap got wrong, rooms or joins. It only puts them back if you go that way again.
  • Check where a new room went on a busy map, and move it somewhere clearer straight away: that helps automap place the next ones well.
  • Moving a join's end: automap reuses a join that leaves from the same side of the room (a south join can start at SSE or SSW, but not SE or SW). Move it to another side and automap draws a new one next time you go that way. Joins for up, down, in and out can use any port.

Next: Settings

items.title: Exporting
items.text:
Back to the guide

Everything is under File > Export. An export writes a whole new file: exporting over a file you've changed since replaces it, changes and all.

items.title: Pictures
items.text:
• Image... saves the map as a picture. PNG is best for maps: sharp, and small for the flat colours of a map. JPEG blurs the lines a little, and BMP files are large.
  • PDF... saves the whole map as one page, as big as it needs to be. It's drawn with lines rather than dots, so it stays sharp however far you zoom in, and you can search its text. Rooms with descriptions carry a note you can open.

A little space is left round the map so nothing at its edge is cut off. To choose how much, set margins for this map in Map Settings > Rooms & Editing, or for every map in App Settings > General (Specify margins).

Smart Save (Ctrl+Alt+S) saves the map, then a PDF and an image of it beside the map file, with the same name, in one go. Choose which, and the image type, in App Settings > General. A map that's never been saved asks for a name first.

items.title: Game source
items.text:
Writing your own game? Recast can write the map out as a starting point, with the rooms, their descriptions, the objects in them and the ways between them:

Language Save to a file Copy to the clipboard Inform 7 Ctrl+Shift+7 Ctrl+Alt+7 Inform 6 Ctrl+Shift+6 Ctrl+Alt+6 TADS Ctrl+Shift+T Ctrl+Alt+T Hugo Ctrl+Shift+H Ctrl+Alt+H ZIL Ctrl+Shift+I Ctrl+Alt+Z Quest Ctrl+Shift+Q Ctrl+Alt+Q (without the header) Alan Ctrl+Shift+L Ctrl+Alt+L Adventuron Ctrl+Alt+A

On a Mac, use Cmd for Ctrl and Option for Alt. Quest to a file is Cmd+Option+Shift+Q, and Hugo to the clipboard is Cmd+Option+Shift+H, as macOS uses the shorter keys itself.

What goes in:

  • Rooms, each with its description, whether it's dark, and which is the start room. Inform 7 groups them by region.
  • Objects, each in its room, or inside the object above it when its line starts with -, with the properties in square brackets (see Objects).
  • Ways between rooms. A join's direction is read from the ports it uses, to the nearest compass point (a join from the east-northeast port goes east), or from its up, down, in or out label. Doors marked in Join Properties become doors in Inform 7 and Inform 6.
  • Names are made safe for each language ("The Porch", "West of the House"), and rooms or objects with the same name each get a name of their own in the code.

Labels are left out: they're notes for you, not part of the game. So are joins that don't reach a room at both ends.

The code is a start, not a finished game: it should build as it is, but you may need to touch some of it up. Inform 7 is the most tried. If an export doesn't build, let us know with the map.

items.title: Inform 7
items.text: Inform 7 keeps a project in a folder ending .inform. Export to a name ending .inform and Recast makes a new project that Inform opens, with the code in Source/Story.ni inside it. To write just the code, choose the Inform 7 Source Files file type and a name ending .ni.

items.title: TADS
items.text: The export writes a .t file. Turn on Save TADS to ADV3Lite (App Settings > General) to write it for the adv3Lite library, with regions.

items.title: Statistics
items.text: Project > Map Statistics... counts the rooms, joins and objects. Export Map Statistics... saves them to a file.

items.title: Editing a map file by hand
items.text:
A .trizbort file is XML, so you can open it in a text editor to change a lot at once: replace a word in every room, or swap one colour for another. Keep a copy first, as Recast may not open a file it doesn't expect.

Next: Keyboard shortcuts

items.title: Getting started
items.text: Back to the guide

items.title: Download and install
items.text:
Get the latest release from the Releases page. The downloads include everything they need: there's no separate .NET to install.

  • Windows: extract TrizbortRecast-<version>-win-x64.zip into a folder you can write to, and run TrizbortRecast.exe. The app isn't signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may warn you the first time: choose More info, then Run anyway.
  • Linux: extract TrizbortRecast-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz and run trizbort-recast. To open .trizbort files from your file manager, see packaging/README.md.
  • macOS: download …-osx-arm64.zip (Apple Silicon) or …-osx-x64.zip (Intel), unzip it and drag Trizbort Recast.app to Applications. The first time, macOS refuses to open it: go to System Settings > Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway.

Recast doesn't update itself. Check the Releases page for new versions.

items.title: Your first map
items.text:
1. Add a room. Double-click an empty part of the map, or press R. Type its name and press Enter.
  2. Add another, a little to the east of the first.
  3. Join them. Hover over the first room: small dots (its ports) appear round its edge. Drag from the east dot to the second room. That's a join: a way from one room to the other.
  4. Save. Press Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on a Mac).

Made a mistake? Ctrl+Z undoes it, and Ctrl+Y puts it back. Every change can be undone.

items.title: Getting around the map
items.text:
• Pan: drag with the right or middle mouse button, hold Space and drag, or scroll with two fingers on a trackpad.
  • Zoom: the mouse wheel, Ctrl+Plus and Ctrl+Minus, or pinch on a trackpad. Ctrl+Home fits the whole map in the window.
  • The minimap in the corner shows the whole map. Click or drag in it to move there.
  • Quick Find (Ctrl+F) finds a room by name.

items.title: Mapping a game for you
items.text:
If your game's interpreter can save a transcript, Recast can draw the map while you play. See Automap.

Next: A quick map, step by step

items.title: Keyboard shortcuts
items.text:
Back to the guide

On a Mac, use Cmd wherever this page says Ctrl. Every shortcut is also shown beside its command in the menus.

items.title: Files
items.text:
Keys Does Ctrl+N New map Ctrl+O Open a map Ctrl+Shift+O Open a map from the web Ctrl+S Save Ctrl+Shift+S Save as Ctrl+Alt+S Smart Save: save, plus a PDF and an image Ctrl+B Save a backup copy

Exports have shortcuts of their own: see Exporting.

items.title: Adding and editing
items.text: Keys Does R Add a room L Add a label B Add a background, behind the selected rooms J Join the selected rooms F2 Rename Alt+Enter Properties Delete or Backspace Delete Alt+Delete Delete all the room's joins Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V Copy, cut, paste Ctrl+D Duplicate Ctrl+Z Undo Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z Redo Esc Cancel a drag, or select nothing

items.title: Rooms
items.text: Keys Does K Dark or lit Ctrl+F5 / Shift+F5 Start room / end room Shift+F2 Change region Ctrl+H, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+8 Straight, elliptical, rounded or octagonal Ctrl+Alt+C Copy the room's colour ; Adjust which ports the joins use W / Ctrl+W / Shift+W / Alt+W Swap two rooms' objects / names / looks / regions Ctrl+Alt+arrow Resize what's selected

items.text: Keys Does P / T Plain / dotted line A One-way arrow V Reverse it U, D, I, O Label it up, down, in or out

items.title: Selecting

items.title: View
items.text: Keys Does Ctrl+Plus / Ctrl+Minus Zoom in / out Ctrl+0 Zoom to 100% Ctrl+Home Fit the whole map in the window Home Reset the view

items.text: Keys Does F10 Next move F9 Previous move F5 Play to the end

items.title: Help and settings
items.text: Keys Does F1 This guide Ctrl+, Application settings Ctrl+Shift+, Map settings

items.title: Labels
items.text:
Back to the guide

Labels are notes on the map: a title, a list of treasures, a reminder of a puzzle. Press L to add one where the mouse is, or right-click and choose Add Label. Double-click a label to edit it.

items.title: Formatting with Markdown
items.text:
Tick Markdown to format the text. You don't need to remember the marks: the toolbar puts them in for you.

  • B, I and <> make the selected words bold, italic or code (Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I).
  • H makes a heading, the list buttons make a bulleted or numbered list, and — draws a line across.
  • Insert Table puts in a small table to type over.
  • Add Link... (Ctrl+K) lists the map's rooms or objects. Search, pick one and press Insert Link, or click a room on the map. Click a room link on the map to go to that room.

On the map, the table above looks like this:

If you'd rather type the marks:

  • Headings: # Treasures, ## Above ground.
  • Bold, italic and code: **bold**, *italic*, `code`.
  • Lists: - lamp, or 1. first. Put two spaces before a line for a list inside a list.
  • A line across: ---.
  • A table: a row a line, with the cells between |s, and |---|---| under the first row to make it the heading.
  • A link to a room: [[Giant Room]], or [[Giant Room|the giant's room]] to show other words.
  • A web link: [the walkthrough](https://...).

Rooms with the same name ("Maze") have their number in the link: [[Maze#42]]. Right-click a room and choose Copy Room Link to get its link, then paste it into the label.

A Markdown label's text starts at its top left. Older versions of Trizbort show the text as written.

items.title: Styles
items.text:
A label's look comes from a style: "Title", "Note", whatever the map needs. The label's Style tab shows the label's text in each of the map's styles: click the one you want. Change a style and every label using it changes with it.

Edit Styles... opens the styles in Map Settings (see Settings). A style sets the font and size, bold and italic, the text colour, the outline, the background, the shape (straight edges, rounded, ellipse or octagon), and where the text sits across and up and down the label. Usual is as labels have always been: centred, or top left for Markdown.

If one label really must be different, choose Modify this label's appearance.... It's better to make a style, so labels stay alike: Create a New Style... there makes one with the label's look, and the label then uses it. Reset to Style takes the label back to its style. A label changed this way says so on the Style tab, but the controls stay hidden until you choose Modify again.

items.title: Size
items.text:
A label grows as you type, and shrinks back as you delete, but never smaller than you made it. Drag its handles to resize it yourself.

Labels can be joined to rooms: with nothing selected, drag from one of the label's ports to a room. They appear in image and PDF exports, but aren't exported to game source. Select, move, copy and delete them as you would rooms.

Older versions of Trizbort ignore labels. Opening a map with labels in them is safe, but saving it there loses the labels and their joins.

Next: Automap

items.title: Drawing the map
items.text:
Back to the guide

A map is rooms and the joins between them, with labels and backgrounds to explain it. Draw it as you play, or let Automap draw it for you.

The garden lists its objects (the spade is in the wheelbarrow). The cellar is dark. The way out of the window is one way, and the dotted grating is a way not tried yet, bent to keep it clear.

items.title: Rooms
items.text:
• Add a room: double-click an empty spot, press R where the mouse is, or right-click and choose Add Room. With a join selected, R puts the new room in the middle of the join.
  • A new room is the size of the last room you selected. Turn on Apply style to new rooms (Application Settings, Map) and it takes that room's look too: shape, border, colours, region and darkness, but not its name or objects.
  • Move it: drag it, or press the arrow keys. Resize it: drag one of the handles round a selected room, or press Ctrl+Alt+arrow.
  • Rename it: press F2. Its properties: double-click it, or press Alt+Enter.
  • Delete it: press Delete. Its joins go with it. Ctrl+Z brings it back.

Rooms can touch or overlap, and the map goes on as far as you need.

items.title: Room Properties
items.text:
At the top:

  • Name, and a Subtitle drawn under it on the map ("by the pit"). The subtitle isn't exported to game source.
  • Start Room and End Room: where the game starts and ends.
  • Dark: the room is drawn with a dark corner. K turns it on and off on the map.
  • Moves: a lift, a car or a train, a room that takes you with it. Automap shows it at each stop as a copy with its name (see Automap).
  • Don't automap from here: for a maze, or anywhere automap can't follow.

A padlock beside the name means automap drew this room and knows it again by its name and description. Click the padlock to unlock them if you need to change them. Where the game has described the room more than one way, the other descriptions are listed under Also described as.

The dialog opens on the tab you used last:

  • Description & Objects: the room's description (shown when you hover over the room, and exported to game source), and what's in it.
  • Shapes & Lines: the border (solid, dashed, dotted and so on, or none), whether it's drawn hand-drawn or straight, and its shape: straight edges, rounded, an ellipse or an octagon. Rounded corners can each be their own size.
  • Region: which region it's in.
  • Colours: the room's fill, a second fill along one side or corner (water beside a room, say), its border, and its name, subtitle and object text. Leave a colour as Default to take it from the region or the map.

Select several rooms and choose Properties... to set their darkness, shape, lines, region and colours all at once. It has the same tabs as one room's properties, without what only one room can have (its name, description and objects). Anything they differ on shows as Mixed, and stays as each room has it unless you change it.

items.title: Objects
items.text:
Put one object a line. To show that something is inside, on top of, or carried by the object above it, start its line with - (and -- for one inside that):

Mr Jones
- hat
-- hatband
- goldfish bowl
Mrs Jones

Tab and Shift+Tab indent and outdent the line for you. After the name you can add properties in square brackets, such as [c] for a container or [m] for a man: Object syntax above the list shows them all. They're used when exporting to game source and don't show on the map.

On the map the list goes below the room, or wherever the map's default is (Map Settings, Rooms), and moves to another side if that spot would cross a join or another room. Drag a list to put it somewhere else, inside the room too once it's selected. Reset Object List Position (the room's right-click menu, Room) puts it back.

items.title: Hovering over a room
items.text: Hover over a room to see its name, whether it's dark, its region, its description and its objects. Choose what's shown in Application Settings, Tooltips.

items.title: Joins
items.text:
A join is a way from one room to another.

  • Draw one: with nothing selected, hover over a room to see its sixteen ports, the dots round its edge. Drag from a port to a port of another room.
  • Or from the keyboard: select two rooms and press J, or press Ctrl+arrow from a room to join it to the room that way, adding the room if there isn't one.
  • Move an end: select the join, then drag the dot at its end to another port.
  • Delete it: select it and press Delete. Alt+Delete deletes all the joins of the selected room.
  • Tidy where joins meet a room: ; (Adjust Ports) moves them to the ports that face the rooms they go to.

Double-click a join, or press Alt+Enter, for its properties:

  • Text labels each end ("u" and "d" here) and the middle ("pull lever"). The compass button beside each end picks directions to type there (and a spell, in Custom), and the buttons below fill in the usual pairs. Start is the room on the left, or the upper one.
  • One Way Arrow for a way you can't come back along. It points from the start room to the end room; Flip turns it round.
  • Dotted for a way you're not sure of, Split to draw a long join as a short stub at each end ("to Building").
  • Unreliable for a way that doesn't always lead where it's drawn (the game picks at random). Directions only take it when there's no other way.
  • Color, and Door for a door, which can be openable, lockable and so on. Doors are exported to game source.

A label that would sit on a line, a room or another label moves out of the way by itself.

On the map, with a join selected:

Key Does P Plain: solid, two way, no labels T Dotted, or solid again A One way, or two way again V Reverse it, swapping the labels at each end U, D, I, O Label it up and down, down and up, in and out, or out and in

P, T and A also set how the next join you draw starts out.

Bend a join: select it and drag the handle in its middle. Once it's bent, two more handles appear, a quarter of the way along from each end, so you can shape it further. Click a handle and press Delete to take it out.

Split joins: click the label at the end of a stub ("to Building") to go to the room it names, or drag the label to move it. Right-click a split join and choose Bring 'X' to 'Y'... to put the two rooms back side by side.

When you export to game source, a join's ports are read as the nearest compass direction (east-northeast is east), and its labels for up, down, in and out.

items.title: Regions
items.text:
A region is a group of rooms drawn in their own colours: "Above ground", "The cellars". Select some rooms, right-click and choose Set Region, then a region, or Add New Region... to make one for them: name it and choose its colours, and press OK. Change Region (Shift+F2) does the same from the keyboard, and the region list in Properties ends with Add New Region... too.

Rooms not in a region are in No Region. Change or delete regions in Map Settings > Regions. Ctrl+Shift+A selects every room in the regions of the rooms you've selected.

items.title: Backgrounds
items.text:
A background is a coloured shape behind part of the map: the shore, the lighthouse, the cottage. It sets them apart whatever regions the rooms are in.

  • Add one: select the rooms it should go behind and press B (or right-click and choose Add Background). It's drawn round them, with a little to spare. With nothing selected, it goes where the mouse is.
  • Inside a background is map like any other: click rooms on it, double-click to add one, or drag a box round them.
  • Pick it up by its edge, or Alt+click inside it. Drag it to move it (the rooms stay where they are), or drag its handles to resize it. Delete removes it.
  • Its properties (double-click its edge, or Alt+Enter): colour, border, shape, and hand-drawn or straight lines.

items.title: Selecting
items.text:
• Click something to select it. Shift+click adds to what's selected, and Ctrl+click takes away from it. The pointer shows a + or a - while you hold the key.
  • Drag a box from an empty spot to select everything in or touching it. Hold Shift to add to the selection, or Ctrl to take away.
  • Ctrl+A selects everything, and Esc nothing. 0 selects the start room.
  • With nothing selected, Enter selects the room nearest the middle of the window.
  • The number pad (or the arrow keys) moves the selection to the room in that direction, along a join if there is one. Ctrl with it follows the join, joins the room that way, or adds a new room there and opens its properties to name it: a quick way to sketch a map from the keyboard. Shift+arrow selects the join that way.

Most things work on everything selected at once: dragging, Delete, dark (K), the join keys above, region, shape and colours. Dragging rooms brings the joins between them along.

items.title: Moving round the map
items.text:
• Pan: drag with the middle mouse button, or the right one, or hold Space and drag. With nothing selected, the arrow keys pan too. The minimap in the corner shows the whole map: click or drag in it to go there.
  • Zoom: the scroll wheel zooms, or pans on a trackpad (choose which in Application Settings: Scroll wheel / trackpad scroll). Ctrl with the wheel always zooms, and so do Ctrl+Plus and Ctrl+Minus.
  • Ctrl+0 zooms to 100%, Ctrl+Home fits the whole map in the window, and Home goes back to the middle of the map.
  • Quick Find (Ctrl+F) finds a room by name.

items.title: Rearranging
items.text:
On a room's right-click menu:

  • Swap: with two rooms selected, swap their objects (W), names (Ctrl+W), looks (Shift+W) or regions (Alt+W).
  • Rooms > Merge Rooms turns two copies of a place into one: the room selected last keeps the others' joins, descriptions and objects. Split Room... turns one room into two.
  • Rooms > Move to a New Area... moves the selected rooms aside together, so a part of the game (inside the house) has room of its own. It offers to take the rooms beyond them too, and splits the joins left behind.
  • Rooms > Tidy Map... lines the rooms up and untangles the joins: the whole map, or just the rooms you've selected. Rooms you've placed yourself stay where you put them.
  • Arrange brings a room or label to the front, or sends it to the back.

items.title: Directions
items.text:
Need to get from one room to another? Right-click where you want to go and choose Navigate to Here. The Directions panel lists the commands to type, and the route glows on the map.

  • While automapping, the directions start from where you are, and follow you as you play.
  • Otherwise, choose Navigate from Here... on the room to start from.
  • Copy Commands copies them, one a line, to paste into the game.
  • Right-click a step and choose Avoid This Route to go another way.

Next: Labels

items.title: More help and resources
items.text: Back to the guide

items.title: Something wrong, or an idea?
items.text: Report problems and ask for features on GitHub Issues. Have a quick look to see whether it's there already, but don't worry about searching hard. A map, or a transcript for automap problems, helps a lot.

items.title: Maps of games
items.text:
• The IF Archive's maps hold maps of many games, plenty of them .trizbort files. Copy the link to one and open it straight from the web with File > Open Map from Web... (Ctrl+Shift+O). Maps often give away puzzles, so look only if you want to know.
  • If you've mapped a game, you can send your map to the IF Archive for others to use.
  • IFWiki has more about game maps.

items.title: Other mapping tools
items.text: The IF Archive's mapping tools has other ways of mapping games, in case Recast isn't quite what you need.

items.title: Several maps in one PDF
items.text:
Recast's PDF export is one page per map. To put several together (a game's upstairs and downstairs, or maps at the back of a walkthrough), a PDF tool such as pdftk joins them:

pdftk upstairs.pdf downstairs.pdf cat output both.pdf

items.title: The original Trizbort
items.text:
Recast opens and saves the same .trizbort maps as the original Trizbort and Trizbort 2. Their own guide is still here: Using Trizbort.

Back to the guide

items.title: A quick map, step by step
items.text:
Back to the guide

This page builds a small game's map from the keyboard, a few minutes' work: a city, a river, a forest, a desert, lava pits, gold mines and a palace. It shows the quickest ways to add rooms, regions and joins. The finished map is generic-game.trizbort, if you'd like to open it alongside.

items.title: The city
items.text:
1. Ctrl+N for a new map. Point at the middle of the map and press R to add a room, then F2 to name it City Center.
  2. With City Center selected, press Ctrl+Up. A new room appears to the north, joined to it, with its properties open: name it N City and press Enter.
  3. Carry on round in a ring with Ctrl+arrows: Ctrl+Left for NW City, Ctrl+Down for W City and SW City, Ctrl+Right for S City and SE City, Ctrl+Up for E City and NE City. Ctrl+Left from NE City finds N City already there and just joins them.
  4. Now join the middle to the ring. Select City Center and press Ctrl with each arrow: where there's a room that way, Recast joins it and moves the selection there, so press the arrow back the other way (without Ctrl) to return to the middle. The number pad's 7, 9, 1 and 3 do the diagonals the same way.

items.title: A region for the city
items.text:
1. Ctrl+A selects every room.
  2. Right-click one of them and choose Rooms > Set Region > Add New Region.... Name it City, make its fill grey, and press OK. The whole city turns grey.

items.title: Death traps
items.text:
1. Select N City, and Ctrl+Up for City Entry, the way out.
  2. From W City, Ctrl+Left for Behind the Barrel, and somewhere else Varmints' Pub. Players die in both, so mark them.
  3. Select the two (Shift+click adds the second), right-click and add a new region, Trap Rooms, in red. Any death trap you add later goes in it too.

items.title: The river, the shore and the forest
items.text:
1. Ctrl+Up from City Entry for C River, then Ctrl+Left and Ctrl+Right from it for W River and E River. Put them in a blue River region.
  2. Crossing the river takes something clever, so its joins should be dotted. Press T: from now on the joins you add are dotted. Ctrl+Up from each river room for W Shore, C Shore and E Shore, then press P to go back to plain joins.
  3. Ctrl+Up from each shore room for W Forest, C Forest and E Forest. The middle of the forest is dark: select it and press K.

items.title: Lava pits, gold mines and a palace
items.text:
1. Use the number pad with Ctrl (Ctrl+7, 8, 9) to add a Desert beyond the forest, in a region of its own. Its fill doesn't have to be one of the usual colours: pick any.
  2. Add a ring of lava pits to one side and gold mines to the other the same way, each in an orange or yellow region, with PERDITION (a death trap, so into Trap Rooms) at the bottom of the pits.
  3. Some ways can't be walked back: select those joins (Shift+click to pick several) and press A to make them one way.
  4. Ctrl+Up from the Desert for Palace Gates, in a purple Palace region. Purple is dark, so give the region white text (Map Settings > Regions). Add a subtitle, start of palace, in the room's properties.

items.title: Putting mistakes right
items.text:
The palace has a few last tricks: a hall, a throne room, a balcony and two jails.

  • Joins drawn the wrong way round? Labelled up and down (D) when they go down and up? Select them and press V to reverse them. Press it again to watch them flip back.
  • Ctrl+Z undoes anything, a step at a time, and Ctrl+Y does it again.
  • A room that shouldn't be joined: add it with Ctrl+Up and then delete the join (select it, Delete), or add it with R and set its region yourself.
  • Rooms in a tangle? Rooms > Tidy Map... (right-click a room) straightens them out.

The finished map has objects in its rooms too ("Whiner #1"). Add them as you go, or come back afterwards: open each room's properties and list them, one a line. Rooms that look alike can be copied with Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V, or Ctrl+D to duplicate.

You'll find your own favourite ways and shortcuts as you go: Keyboard shortcuts lists them all.

Next: Drawing the map

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Back to the guide

There are two kinds of settings:

  • App settings (Edit > Application Settings..., Ctrl+,) are yours: they apply to every map you open.
  • Map settings (Edit > Map Settings..., Ctrl+Shift+,) are saved in the map, so anyone who opens it sees it the same way. A new map starts with the defaults; Edit > Restore Default Map Settings puts them back (one undo step).

items.title: App settings
items.text:
General:

  • Save images at 100%: export pictures at full size, whatever the zoom.
  • Open last project on start, and Keep a recovery copy of unsaved changes (on by default) in case Recast closes before you save.
  • Invert Mouse Wheel Zoom, and Scroll wheel / trackpad scroll: Automatic zooms with a mouse wheel and pans with a trackpad, or choose Always zoom or Always pan. Ctrl with the wheel always zooms.
  • Show Full Path in Title Bar.
  • Port Adjust Detail: how many ports Adjust Ports (;) chooses from: the four sides, the corners too, or all sixteen.
  • Smart Save: whether Smart Save (Ctrl+Alt+S) also saves a PDF and an image, and which image type. Save TADS to ADV3Lite writes TADS exports for the adv3Lite library.
  • App defaults: the font for new maps, and margins round exported pictures (unless a map sets its own).

Tooltips: whether hovering over the map shows tooltips, and whether they include objects and descriptions (and how many letters of a description).

Map:

  • Apply style to new rooms makes each new room copy the look of the last room you selected.
  • Where you are: the token that marks where you are while automapping: a wooden disc, a brass coin, a pawn, a "you are here" sign, painted or pewter figures, or your own (a PNG with a transparent background, or an SVG). Untick Token on the room to hide it. Glow round the room sets the colour of the glow.

items.title: Map Details
items.text: The map's title, author, description and history. They're saved in the map, and game source exports use them: the title and author for the game's name and byline, and the description as its headline.

items.title: Lines & Grid
items.text:
• Hand-drawn style gives the whole map a sketched look: rooms, joins and labels drawn with a gentle pen-like wobble. A room can be set straight or hand-drawn in its own properties.
  • Width of lines, and Arrow Size on one-way joins.
  • Room Arrow Stalk Length: a join leaves a room straight out from its port for this far before heading off.
  • Text Offset From Line: the gap between a join and its labels.
  • Preferred Distance Between Rooms: how far apart automap and Ctrl+arrow put new rooms.
  • Join labels: whether to write the direction at the end of a join leaving from a side (N, E, S, W) or a corner (NE, SE, SW, NW) when it has no label of its own, and whether to show up and down. Direction words draws directions "n" or "north" (or as written), whichever way each label was typed. Only the drawing changes. The preview shows the result.
  • Grid: shown or not, its size, whether rooms and joins snap to it, and a faint cross at the middle of the map (Show Origin).

items.title: Rooms & Editing
items.text:
• Default Room Text, the name a new room starts with, and its Default Shape.
  • Darkness Stripe Size: the dark corner on a dark room.
  • Object List Offset, and Object List Position: drag the sample list to where object lists go, beside a side or corner of the room or inside it.
  • Advanced: the size of handles and ports, and how near you must click to pick something (Snap to Element Distance). Make it bigger if things are hard to pick up.
  • Margins: Wrap Text at Dashes, and margins round this map's exported pictures.

items.title: Colours
items.text: The map's colours: the canvas, room borders, joins (and joins selected or under the mouse, which don't show in exports), subtitle, object and join text, the grid, and the start and end rooms. Rooms take their fill and name colour from their region.

items.title: Fonts
items.text: The fonts for room names, objects, joins and subtitles. Someone opening the map without a font sees another one instead.

items.title: Regions
items.text: Add Region, Delete Region (its rooms go to No Region), and each region's name, fill and text colour. No Region can't be renamed, but you can change its colours. Region names can't differ only in capitals. A dark fill needs a light text colour: Recast leaves that to you.

items.title: Styles
items.text:
The map's label styles. Every map has Default. New Style makes one based on the style that's selected: it looks the same until you change something. What it doesn't set comes from the style it's based on, and the tab says where ("from Title"). Reset takes a value from there again. Delete a style and its labels take the style it was based on.

Styles are saved in the map. Older versions draw each label as it looks now.

items.title: Themes
items.text:
A theme changes the whole look of a map in one go: Classic, Parchment, Dark, High contrast or Sketch. Choose Edit > Map Theme....

  • A theme sets the map's colours, fonts, region colours, default room shape, hand-drawn style, line sizes, grid and margins. It never changes your rooms, joins, names or layout. Regions are matched by name.
  • Reset individual room/line styles also clears colours and shapes you've set on single rooms and joins.
  • Export Selected Theme... and Export Current Map Theme... save a .trizbort-theme file to share, and Import Theme... reads one. A theme needs its fonts installed.
  • Infer Default Room Style... helps when every room was styled by hand: it finds the look most rooms share and makes it the map's default, so a theme exported afterwards carries it. A preview lists the changes first.

Applying a theme is one undo step.

Next: Exporting

items.title: What's new
items.text:
Back to the guide

The highlights of each release, newest first. Every change is listed in the changelog.

items.title: Coming next
items.text:
• Label styles. Choose a style for each label, such as "Title" or "Note", with its font and size, colours, outline, background and shape. A style can be based on another. Change a style and its labels change too. See Labels.
  • Backgrounds: coloured shapes behind parts of the map, to set them apart. Select some rooms and press B. See Drawing the map.
  • Add New Region... on a room's Set Region menu makes a region for the selected rooms, and the default region is called No Region.
  • Directions know a magic word back once you've used it both ways ("xyzzy" there and back).
  • Automap's guesses read more plainly: an untried way is "unexplored", a way that comes back says it looks like a loop, and Wrong Room: Choose... shows a new room beside the room you left.
  • Assume joins go both ways is the new name for "Always assume two-way connections", and each option in the automapping dialog has an ⓘ to hover over for more about it.
  • A shorter automapping dialog. The game screen is shown or hidden on the automap panel, and join labels follow the map's Direction words setting.

items.title: 0.15 (22 November 2026)
items.text:
You are here. The room automap has you in carries a token, like a playing piece on a board, and glows. Drag the token to put automap right. Choose your token in App Settings, or load your own.

Markdown labels. Headings, bold, lists, tables, and links to rooms you can click. A toolbar puts the marks in for you, and the label grows to fit.

Automap says when it guessed. When it picks a room for you and it could be another, the panel says what it guessed and why, with Wrong Room: Choose... to fix it.

Also: Unreliable joins for ways that don't always lead the same place, and Split Room now draws both rooms as the map does.

items.title: 0.14 (16 November 2026)
items.text:
Directions, like a satnav: right-click a room and choose Navigate to Here. The route glows on the map, and follows you as you play.

Also: Automap Settings can be changed while automap runs (the ⚙ on the panel), Play to the End shows its progress, and each tidy is an undo step of its own.

items.title: 0.13 (15 November 2026)
items.text:
The map rethinks itself. When a move shows the map was laid out the wrong way round, automap lays it out again, and the rooms slide to their new places. Layouts are tidier and better balanced, and rooms you placed yourself stay put.

Split Room... for a room that turns out to be two places with one name, and a bigger game screen in the automap panel.

items.title: 0.12 (10 November 2026)
items.text:
The automap panel gathers automap's controls beside the map: where you are, the transcript, and mapping or tracking only.

Also: rooms that move (lifts, cars), Merge Rooms, Split Join to tidy away long joins, darkness, and Which room does it mean? showing the room you pick on the map behind it.

items.title: 0.11 (8 November 2026)
items.text: Renamed Trizbort: Recast. Rooms tidy themselves as you explore, and Tidy Map... tidies the whole map. Play a transcript move by move, and watch the game on a small game screen.

items.title: 0.10 (2 November 2026)
items.text: Recovery copies of your unsaved work after a crash, and plainer error messages. Automap follows magic words (xyzzy) and lists several ways between two rooms on one join.

items.title: 0.9 (31 October 2026)
items.text: The first beta of Recast: the same app on Windows, Linux and macOS. Undo and redo for every change, trackpads and touchscreens, and sharp, searchable PDF export.

items.title: Before Recast
items.text: Trizbort 2 added map labels, curved joins and themes to the original Windows app. See the original guide.
